topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, introduces the topic of the complement system, and frames its complexity and nomenclature.

topics.label: Fundamentals and general principles of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overview of complement's primary roles, explain its naming conventions, and detail the central biochemical function of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three activation pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—and the threshold required to trigger the cascade.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which complement eliminates pathogens, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms and proteins that protect host cells from unintended complement attack.

topics.label: Clinical presentations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in specific complement components lead to distinct clinical outcomes and disease susceptibilities.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and practical applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the strategies pathogens use to escape complement-mediated clearance and the clinical and laboratory uses of staphylococcal protein A.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion on complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
